# auth

sign in to Coder and manage saved server sessions

## `auth login [--server <server>] [--workspace <workspace>] [--yes] [--device] [--json]`

sign in through the browser

Sign in with Wular Auth in your browser. The CLI keeps the tokens in ~/.coder/session.json, and commands that talk to a server then act as you.

- `--server <server>` act on your Coder server
- `--workspace <workspace>` with --server: the workspace to act in (default: the saved one)
- `--yes` with --server: connect to a server used for the first time without asking
- `--device` show a code to approve on another device; the default without a local browser
- `--json` JSON output

Environment:

- `CODER_SERVER` the server to use instead of https://coder.wular.ai

```sh
coder auth login  # sign in to the hosted service
coder auth login --server https://agents.example.com  # sign in to a self-hosted server
```

## `auth logout [--server <server>] [--yes] [--json]`

sign out and forget the saved session

Revoke the saved session for that server at Wular Auth and forget its tokens.

- `--server <server>` sign out of this Coder server (default: the hosted one)
- `--yes` connect to a server used for the first time without asking
- `--json` JSON output

## `auth status [--json]`

show where you are signed in

List saved sessions with their server, user, and workspace.

- `--json` JSON output

Environment:

- `CODER_SERVER` the server to use instead of https://coder.wular.ai
